bodyMarkdown:
## Property Manager Salary: Understanding the Conversion

If you are a property manager or considering the role, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or checking your pay against award minimums, the basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. This article explains the conversion, the role of the 38-hour week, and how tax and superannuation fit in.

### The Standard 38-Hour Week

Most full-time property managers work a 38-hour week, as set by the Real Estate Industry Award and the National Employment Standards. When converting an hourly rate to an annual figure, we assume 38 hours per week unless your contract states otherwise. The formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, a property manager earning $30 per hour would have an annual salary of $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 before tax and super. This is the gross amount; your take-home pay will be lower after tax and the Medicare levy.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many property managers are paid fortnightly or weekly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $30/hour rate:

- Weekly: $30 × 38 = $1,140
- Fortnightly: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280

These figures are before any deductions. If you are a casual property manager, you receive a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For a casual earning $30/hour base, the loaded rate is $37.50/hour. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator – always start with the base rate and add the loading separately.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. However, property managers are typically covered by the Real Estate Industry Award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award, including the Real Estate Industry Award. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. A Level 1 property manager might earn around $24.80 per hour (exact rates depend on classification and experience). Always check the award pay guide for your specific role.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual property managers receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. The loading is paid on top of the base rate, not included in it. For example, if the award base rate is $24.80, the casual rate is $31.00 per hour.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a property manager earning $30/hour, the employer contributes an additional $3.60 per hour to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra benefit.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income between $18,201 and $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a property manager earning $59,280 annually, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $9,700, leaving a take-home pay of about $49,580 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains the math in more detail.

### What About Average Earnings?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. Many property managers earn less than this average, especially those starting out or working part-time. The all-employees total earnings figure of $1,579.20 per week includes part-time workers, so it is lower. Your property manager salary will depend on your award classification, experience, and location.

### Key Takeaways

- Use the formula: hourly rate × 38 × 52 for annual gross.
- Fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top, up to the contribution cap.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay.
- Check the Real Estate Industry Award pay guide for minimum rates.

For a full breakdown of your specific situation, explore our [reference tables](/data) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) resources.
